about: Microsoft SQL Server / Azure SQL (T-SQL) built-in vocabulary, also used for MS Access connections. Merged over common.json; entries here with the same name replace the common entry.

functions.name: APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT
functions.summary: Returns the approximate number of unique non-null values in a group, using far less memory than COUNT(DISTINCT) on large data sets.

params.name: expression
params.doc: The values to count; NULLs are ignored.

functions.name: APPROX_PERCENTILE_CONT
functions.summary: Returns an approximate interpolated percentile of the sorted values in a group, written with WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...). (SQL Server 2022+)

params.name: percentile
params.doc: A constant between 0.0 and 1.0, such as 0.5 for the median.

functions.name: APPROX_PERCENTILE_DISC
functions.summary: Returns an approximate percentile value that actually exists in the sorted group, written with WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...). (SQL Server 2022+)

signatures.returns: same type as the ORDER BY expression

params.name: percentile
params.doc: A constant between 0.0 and 1.0, such as 0.9 for the 90th percentile.

functions.name: CHECKSUM_AGG
functions.summary: Returns a checksum of the integer values in a group, useful for detecting changes in a table or column.
functions.example: SELECT CHECKSUM_AGG(CAST(Quantity AS int)) FROM Production.ProductInventory

params.name: [ALL | DISTINCT] expression
params.doc: An integer expression; DISTINCT checksums unique values only.

functions.name: COUNT_BIG
functions.summary: Returns the number of items in a group as a bigint; works like COUNT but cannot overflow int.

params.name: * | [ALL | DISTINCT] expression
params.doc: Use * to count rows, or an expression to count its non-null values.

functions.name: GROUPING
functions.summary: Returns 1 when the column in a ROLLUP, CUBE or GROUPING SETS row is aggregated (a subtotal), 0 when it is a regular grouped value.
functions.example: SELECT Region, SUM(Total), GROUPING(Region) FROM Sales GROUP BY ROLLUP(Region)

params.name: column_expression
params.doc: A column or expression listed in the GROUP BY clause.

functions.name: GROUPING_ID
functions.summary: Returns a bitmask integer showing which of the listed GROUP BY columns are aggregated in the current row.

params.name: column_expression
params.doc: A column that appears in the GROUP BY clause; the leftmost column is the highest bit.

functions.name: STDEV
functions.summary: Returns the statistical sample standard deviation of the values in a group.

params.name: [ALL | DISTINCT] expression
params.doc: A numeric expression; NULLs are ignored.

functions.name: STDEVP
functions.summary: Returns the statistical population standard deviation of the values in a group.

params.name: [ALL | DISTINCT] expression
params.doc: A numeric expression; NULLs are ignored.

functions.name: VAR
functions.summary: Returns the statistical sample variance of the values in a group.

params.name: [ALL | DISTINCT] expression
params.doc: A numeric expression; NULLs are ignored.

functions.name: VARP
functions.summary: Returns the statistical population variance of the values in a group.

params.name: [ALL | DISTINCT] expression
params.doc: A numeric expression; NULLs are ignored.

functions.name: STRING_AGG
functions.summary: Concatenates the non-null string values of a group, putting the separator between them. Add WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...) to control the order.

signatures.returns: nvarchar or varchar (max when the input is max)

params.name: expression
params.doc: The values to concatenate; other types are converted to strings.

params.name: separator
params.doc: Literal or variable placed between values, such as ', '.

functions.name: PRODUCT
functions.summary: Returns the product of all values in a group (or window). (SQL Server 2025+ and Azure SQL)

signatures.returns: same numeric type family as expression

params.name: [ALL | DISTINCT] expression
params.doc: A numeric expression; NULLs are ignored.

functions.name: JSON_ARRAYAGG
functions.summary: Builds a JSON array from the values of a group; optional ORDER BY and NULL ON NULL / ABSENT ON NULL go inside the parentheses. (SQL Server 2025+ and Azure SQL)
functions.example: SELECT JSON_ARRAYAGG(Name ORDER BY Name) FROM dbo.Tags

params.name: value_expression [ORDER BY ...] [NULL ON NULL | ABSENT ON NULL]
params.doc: The value added to the array for each row, with optional ordering and NULL handling.

functions.name: JSON_OBJECTAGG
functions.summary: Builds a JSON object from key:value pairs taken from each row of a group. (SQL Server 2025+ and Azure SQL)

params.name: key : value [NULL ON NULL | ABSENT ON NULL]
params.doc: The property name and value contributed by each row, with optional NULL handling.

functions.name: PERCENTILE_CONT
functions.summary: Returns an interpolated percentile of the sorted values; written with WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...) and OVER ([PARTITION BY ...]).
functions.example: PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY Rate) OVER (PARTITION BY DeptID)

params.name: percentile
params.doc: A constant between 0.0 and 1.0, such as 0.5 for the median.

functions.name: PERCENTILE_DISC
functions.summary: Returns the first sorted value whose cumulative distribution reaches the percentile; written with WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...) and OVER ([PARTITION BY ...]).
functions.example: PERCENTILE_DISC(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY Rate) OVER (PARTITION BY DeptID)

signatures.returns: same type as the ORDER BY expression

params.name: percentile
params.doc: A constant between 0.0 and 1.0, such as 0.5 for the median.

functions.name: ASCII
functions.summary: Returns the ASCII code of the first character of a string.

params.name: character_expression
params.doc: The string whose first character is converted.

functions.name: CHAR
functions.summary: Returns the single-byte character for an integer code from 0 to 255; NULL outside that range.

functions.name: CHARINDEX
functions.summary: Returns the 1-based position of the first occurrence of one string inside another, or 0 when it is not found.

params.name: start_location
params.doc: Position to start searching from; 0 or negative starts at the beginning.

functions.name: CONCAT
functions.summary: Joins two or more values into one string. NULLs are treated as empty strings and non-string values are converted implicitly.

params.name: string_value2
params.doc: The next value to join; more may follow.

functions.name: CONCAT_WS
functions.summary: Joins two or more values with a separator between them, skipping NULL values.

params.name: separator
params.doc: The text placed between each pair of values.

params.name: argument2
params.doc: The next value to join; more may follow.

functions.name: DATALENGTH
functions.summary: Returns the number of bytes used to store a value, including trailing spaces; nvarchar uses 2 bytes per character.

functions.name: DIFFERENCE
functions.summary: Compares the SOUNDEX codes of two strings and returns 0 (no similarity) to 4 (strong similarity).

functions.name: FORMAT
functions.summary: Formats a date/time or number using a .NET format string and an optional culture, such as 'yyyy-MM-dd' or 'N2'.

params.name: format
params.doc: A .NET standard or custom format pattern, such as 'd', 'C' or 'dd/MM/yyyy'.

params.name: culture
params.doc: A culture name such as 'en-US' or 'de-DE'; defaults to the session language.

functions.name: LEFT
functions.summary: Returns the given number of characters from the start of a string.

functions.name: LEN
functions.summary: Returns the number of characters in a string, excluding trailing spaces. Use DATALENGTH for bytes.

functions.name: LTRIM
functions.summary: Removes leading spaces, or with a second argument (SQL Server 2022+) any of the given characters, from the start of a string.

params.name: characters
params.doc: The set of characters to remove instead of spaces. (SQL Server 2022+)

functions.name: RTRIM
functions.summary: Removes trailing spaces, or with a second argument (SQL Server 2022+) any of the given characters, from the end of a string.

params.name: characters
params.doc: The set of characters to remove instead of spaces. (SQL Server 2022+)

functions.name: TRIM
functions.summary: Removes spaces, or the listed characters, from both ends of a string. The LEADING, TRAILING and BOTH forms are SQL Server 2022+.

params.name: characters FROM string
params.doc: The characters to remove from both ends, FROM, then the string to trim.

params.name: {LEADING | TRAILING | BOTH} [characters] FROM string
params.doc: Which end to trim, optional characters to remove (default space), FROM, then the string. (SQL Server 2022+)

functions.name: NCHAR
functions.summary: Returns the Unicode character for an integer code point.

functions.name: PATINDEX
functions.summary: Returns the 1-based position of the first match of a LIKE-style pattern in a string, or 0 when there is none.

params.name: '%pattern%'
params.doc: A LIKE pattern; wildcards %, _, [ ] and [^] are allowed and it usually starts and ends with %.

functions.name: QUOTENAME
functions.summary: Wraps a string in delimiters so it is a valid SQL Server identifier, doubling any embedded closing delimiters.

params.name: character_string
params.doc: The name to quote, up to 128 characters; longer input returns NULL.

params.name: quote_character
params.doc: The delimiter: '[' or ']' (default), a single quote, a double quote, '(', ')', '<', '>', '{', '}' or '`'.

functions.name: REPLICATE
functions.summary: Repeats a string the given number of times.

params.name: integer_expression
params.doc: How many times to repeat it; negative returns NULL.

functions.name: REVERSE
functions.summary: Returns a string with its characters in reverse order.

functions.name: RIGHT
functions.summary: Returns the given number of characters from the end of a string.

functions.name: SOUNDEX
functions.summary: Returns a four-character code representing how a string sounds in English, for fuzzy name matching.

functions.name: SPACE
functions.summary: Returns a string of repeated spaces.

params.name: integer_expression
params.doc: How many spaces; negative returns NULL.

functions.name: STR
functions.summary: Converts a number to right-aligned character data with a given total length and number of decimal places.

params.name: length
params.doc: Total length including sign, digits and decimal point; default 10.

params.name: decimal
params.doc: Digits to the right of the decimal point, up to 16; default 0.

functions.name: STRING_ESCAPE
functions.summary: Escapes special characters in text for the given target format; currently only 'json' is supported.

params.name: type
params.doc: The escaping rules to apply; must be 'json'.

functions.name: STRING_SPLIT
functions.summary: Splits a string into rows of substrings on a single-character separator, returning a table with a value column (and ordinal when enabled).

params.name: separator
params.doc: The single character that separates items.

params.name: enable_ordinal
params.doc: 1 adds an ordinal column with each item's 1-based position. (SQL Server 2022+)

functions.name: STUFF
functions.summary: Deletes a run of characters from a string and inserts another string at the same position.

params.name: start
params.doc: 1-based position where deletion and insertion begin.

params.name: length
params.doc: How many characters to delete; 0 inserts without deleting.

functions.name: SUBSTRING
functions.summary: Returns part of a character, binary, text or image value, starting at a 1-based position.

params.name: start
params.doc: 1-based position of the first character to return.

params.name: length
params.doc: How many characters to return; omitting it returns the rest (SQL Server 2025+ and Azure SQL).

functions.name: TRANSLATE
functions.summary: Replaces each character in the second argument with the character at the same position in the third, throughout the input string.

params.name: translations
params.doc: The replacement characters; must be the same length as characters.

functions.name: UNICODE
functions.summary: Returns the Unicode code point of the first character of a string.

params.name: ncharacter_expression
params.doc: The string whose first character is converted.

functions.name: UNISTR
functions.summary: Returns a Unicode string built from text containing \xxxx or \+xxxxxx escape sequences. (SQL Server 2025+ and Azure SQL)

params.name: unicode_escape_character
params.doc: The escape character to use instead of backslash.

functions.name: BASE64_ENCODE
functions.summary: Encodes a varbinary value as Base64 text. (SQL Server 2025+ and Azure SQL)

params.name: url_safe
params.doc: 1 uses the URL-safe alphabet without padding.

functions.name: BASE64_DECODE
functions.summary: Decodes Base64 text back into a varbinary value. (SQL Server 2025+ and Azure SQL)

functions.name: REGEXP_LIKE
functions.summary: Returns true when a string matches a regular expression; used as a predicate in WHERE, CHECK and similar clauses. (SQL Server 2025+ and Azure SQL)

params.name: flags
params.doc: Match flags: 'i' case-insensitive, 'c' case-sensitive, 'm' multi-line, 's' dot matches newline.

functions.name: REGEXP_REPLACE
functions.summary: Replaces matches of a regular expression with a replacement string. (SQL Server 2025+ and Azure SQL)

params.name: string_replacement
params.doc: The replacement text; \1 to \9 refer to groups. Default is empty.

params.name: start
params.doc: 1-based position to start searching from; default 1.

params.name: occurrence
params.doc: Which match to replace; 0 (default) replaces all.

params.name: flags
params.doc: Match flags: 'i' case-insensitive, 'c' case-sensitive, 'm' multi-line, 's' dot matches newline.

functions.name: REGEXP_SUBSTR
functions.summary: Returns the substring that matches a regular expression, or NULL when there is no match. (SQL Server 2025+ and Azure SQL)

params.name: start
params.doc: 1-based position to start searching from; default 1.

params.name: flags
params.doc: Match flags: 'i' case-insensitive, 'c' case-sensitive, 'm' multi-line, 's' dot matches newline.

params.name: group
params.doc: Capture group to return; 0 (default) returns the whole match.

functions.name: REGEXP_INSTR
functions.summary: Returns the start or end position of a regular expression match, or 0 when there is none. (SQL Server 2025+ and Azure SQL)

params.name: start
params.doc: 1-based position to start searching from; default 1.

params.name: return_option
params.doc: 0 (default) returns the match start, 1 the position after the match.

params.name: flags
params.doc: Match flags: 'i' case-insensitive, 'c' case-sensitive, 'm' multi-line, 's' dot matches newline.

params.name: group
params.doc: Capture group to locate; 0 (default) uses the whole match.

functions.name: REGEXP_COUNT
functions.summary: Returns how many times a regular expression matches in a string. (SQL Server 2025+ and Azure SQL)

params.name: start
params.doc: 1-based position to start searching from; default 1.

params.name: flags
params.doc: Match flags: 'i' case-insensitive, 'c' case-sensitive, 'm' multi-line, 's' dot matches newline.

functions.name: REGEXP_MATCHES
functions.summary: Returns a table with one row per regular expression match, including the matched text, its position and capture groups. (SQL Server 2025+ and Azure SQL)

params.name: flags
params.doc: Match flags: 'i' case-insensitive, 'c' case-sensitive, 'm' multi-line, 's' dot matches newline.

functions.name: REGEXP_SPLIT_TO_TABLE
functions.summary: Splits a string on a regular expression and returns one row per piece with its ordinal. (SQL Server 2025+ and Azure SQL)

params.name: pattern_expression
params.doc: The regular expression that matches separators (RE2 syntax).

params.name: flags
params.doc: Match flags: 'i' case-insensitive, 'c' case-sensitive, 'm' multi-line, 's' dot matches newline.

functions.name: ACOS
functions.summary: Returns the angle in radians whose cosine is the given number.

functions.name: ASIN
functions.summary: Returns the angle in radians whose sine is the given number.

functions.name: ATAN
functions.summary: Returns the angle in radians whose tangent is the given number.

functions.name: ATN2
functions.summary: Returns the angle in radians between the positive x-axis and the ray to the point (x, y).

functions.name: CEILING
functions.summary: Returns the smallest integer greater than or equal to a number.

functions.name: COS
functions.summary: Returns the cosine of an angle given in radians.

functions.name: COT
functions.summary: Returns the cotangent of an angle given in radians.

functions.name: DEGREES
functions.summary: Converts an angle from radians to degrees.

functions.name: EXP
functions.summary: Returns e raised to the given power.

functions.name: FLOOR
functions.summary: Returns the largest integer less than or equal to a number.

functions.name: LOG
functions.summary: Returns the natural logarithm of a number, or its logarithm in the given base.

params.name: float_expression
params.doc: The number; must be greater than 0.

params.name: base
params.doc: The logarithm base; natural log (base e) when omitted.

functions.name: LOG10
functions.summary: Returns the base-10 logarithm of a number.

params.name: float_expression
params.doc: The number; must be greater than 0.

functions.name: PI
functions.summary: Returns the constant pi (3.14159265358979).

functions.name: POWER
functions.summary: Returns a number raised to the given power.

functions.name: RADIANS
functions.summary: Converts an angle from degrees to radians.

params.name: numeric_expression
params.doc: The angle in degrees; pass a decimal or float to avoid integer truncation.

functions.name: RAND
functions.summary: Returns a pseudo-random float from 0 through 1 (exclusive). It is evaluated once per query, not per row.

params.name: seed
params.doc: A seed value; the same seed gives the same sequence.

functions.name: ROUND
functions.summary: Rounds a number to the given number of decimal places, or truncates it when the third argument is non-zero.

params.name: length
params.doc: Decimal places to keep; negative rounds to the left of the decimal point.

functions.name: SIGN
functions.summary: Returns -1, 0 or 1 for a negative, zero or positive number.

functions.name: SIN
functions.summary: Returns the sine of an angle given in radians.

functions.name: SQRT
functions.summary: Returns the square root of a number.

params.name: float_expression
params.doc: The number; must not be negative.

functions.name: SQUARE
functions.summary: Returns the square of a number.

functions.name: TAN
functions.summary: Returns the tangent of an angle given in radians.

functions.name: GREATEST
functions.summary: Returns the largest value from a list of expressions, ignoring NULLs; the result type is the highest-precedence argument type. (SQL Server 2022+)

params.name: expression
params.doc: A value to compare; 1 to 254 arguments.

functions.name: LEAST
functions.summary: Returns the smallest value from a list of expressions, ignoring NULLs; the result type is the highest-precedence argument type. (SQL Server 2022+)

params.name: expression
params.doc: A value to compare; 1 to 254 arguments.

functions.name: BIT_COUNT
functions.summary: Returns the number of bits set to 1 in an integer or binary value. (SQL Server 2022+)

params.name: expression_value
params.doc: The value whose set bits are counted.

functions.name: GET_BIT
functions.summary: Returns the bit (0 or 1) at the given offset of an integer or binary value. (SQL Server 2022+)

params.name: bit_offset
params.doc: Zero-based bit position, counting from the least significant bit.

functions.name: SET_BIT
functions.summary: Returns the value with the bit at the given offset set to 1, or to the given bit value. (SQL Server 2022+)

params.name: bit_offset
params.doc: Zero-based bit position, counting from the least significant bit.

functions.name: LEFT_SHIFT
functions.summary: Shifts the bits of an integer or binary value left by the given number of positions. (SQL Server 2022+)

params.name: shift_amount
params.doc: How many bit positions to shift.

functions.name: RIGHT_SHIFT
functions.summary: Shifts the bits of an integer or binary value right by the given number of positions. (SQL Server 2022+)

params.name: shift_amount
params.doc: How many bit positions to shift.

functions.name: CURRENT_DATE
functions.summary: Returns the current database system date as a date value, without time. (SQL Server 2025+ and Azure SQL)

functions.name: CURRENT_TIMEZONE
functions.summary: Returns the name of the time zone the server or instance is set to.

functions.name: CURRENT_TIMEZONE_ID
functions.summary: Returns the Windows time zone ID the server or instance is set to, such as 'UTC'. (SQL Server 2022+ and Azure SQL)

functions.name: DATEADD
functions.summary: Adds a number of date-part units to a date and returns the result.

params.name: datepart
params.doc: The unit to add, such as year, month, day or minute (weekday and dayofyear add days).

params.name: number
params.doc: How many units to add; negative subtracts. Fractions are truncated.

params.name: date
params.doc: The date or time value to add to.

functions.name: DATEDIFF
functions.summary: Returns the number of date-part boundaries crossed between a start and an end date, as an int.

params.name: datepart
params.doc: The unit to count, such as day, month or second.

params.name: enddate
params.doc: The ending date or time; the result is negative when it is before startdate.

functions.name: DATEDIFF_BIG
functions.summary: Returns the number of date-part boundaries crossed between two dates as a bigint, for large differences such as nanoseconds.

params.name: datepart
params.doc: The unit to count, such as millisecond or nanosecond.

functions.name: DATEPART
functions.summary: Returns an integer for the given part of a date, such as the year, month or weekday.

params.name: datepart
params.doc: The part to return; weekday depends on SET DATEFIRST, iso_week follows ISO 8601.

params.name: date
params.doc: The date or time value to read.

functions.name: DATENAME
functions.summary: Returns the given part of a date as a string, such as the month or weekday name in the session language.

params.name: datepart
params.doc: The part to return, such as month or weekday.

params.name: date
params.doc: The date or time value to read.

functions.name: DATETRUNC
functions.summary: Truncates a date to the start of the given date part, such as the first day of its month. (SQL Server 2022+)

params.name: datepart
params.doc: The precision to truncate to; week uses SET DATEFIRST, iso_week starts on Monday.

params.name: date
params.doc: The date or time value to truncate.

functions.name: DATE_BUCKET
functions.summary: Returns the start of the fixed-width time bucket that contains a date, measured from an origin. (SQL Server 2022+)

params.name: datepart
params.doc: The unit of the bucket width.

params.name: number
params.doc: The bucket width in datepart units; must be positive.

params.name: date
params.doc: The date or time value to place in a bucket.

params.name: origin
params.doc: The bucket origin, same type as date; default 1900-01-01 00:00:00.

functions.name: DATEFROMPARTS
functions.summary: Builds a date from year, month and day numbers.

functions.name: DATETIME2FROMPARTS
functions.summary: Builds a datetime2 value from its parts with the given fractional-second precision.

params.name: fractions
params.doc: The fractional seconds, scaled by precision (e.g. 5 with precision 1 is 0.5 s).

params.name: precision
params.doc: Fractional-second precision, 0 to 7; must be a literal.

functions.name: DATETIMEFROMPARTS
functions.summary: Builds a datetime value from its parts.

functions.name: DATETIMEOFFSETFROMPARTS
functions.summary: Builds a datetimeoffset value from its parts, a UTC offset and a fractional-second precision.

params.name: fractions
params.doc: The fractional seconds, scaled by precision.

params.name: hour_offset
params.doc: The hour part of the time zone offset, -14 to 14.

params.name: minute_offset
params.doc: The minute part of the time zone offset.

params.name: precision
params.doc: Fractional-second precision, 0 to 7; must be a literal.

functions.name: SMALLDATETIMEFROMPARTS
functions.summary: Builds a smalldatetime value from its parts.

functions.name: TIMEFROMPARTS
functions.summary: Builds a time value from its parts with the given fractional-second precision.

params.name: fractions
params.doc: The fractional seconds, scaled by precision.

params.name: precision
params.doc: Fractional-second precision, 0 to 7; must be a literal.

functions.name: DAY
functions.summary: Returns the day of the month (1 to 31) of a date.

functions.name: MONTH
functions.summary: Returns the month number (1 to 12) of a date.

functions.name: YEAR
functions.summary: Returns the year of a date.

functions.name: EOMONTH
functions.summary: Returns the last day of the month containing a date, optionally shifted by a number of months.

params.name: start_date
params.doc: The date whose month is used.

params.name: month_to_add
params.doc: Months to add before finding the month end; may be negative.

functions.name: GETDATE
functions.summary: Returns the current date and time of the server as a datetime value (local time, about 3 ms precision).

functions.name: GETUTCDATE
functions.summary: Returns the current UTC date and time as a datetime value.

functions.name: SYSDATETIME
functions.summary: Returns the current date and time of the server as a high-precision datetime2(7) value.

functions.name: SYSUTCDATETIME
functions.summary: Returns the current UTC date and time as a high-precision datetime2(7) value.

functions.name: SYSDATETIMEOFFSET
functions.summary: Returns the current date and time of the server including its UTC offset.

functions.name: SWITCHOFFSET
functions.summary: Returns a datetimeoffset value converted to a different time zone offset, keeping the same instant.

params.name: timezoneoffset_expression
params.doc: The new offset as '[+|-]hh:mm' or as minutes.

functions.name: TODATETIMEOFFSET
functions.summary: Attaches a time zone offset to a date/time value without changing its clock time.

params.name: timezoneoffset_expression
params.doc: The offset as '[+|-]hh:mm' or as minutes.

functions.name: ISDATE
functions.summary: Returns 1 when a string is a valid date, time or datetime (not datetime2) under the current DATEFORMAT and language, else 0.

params.name: expression
params.doc: The value to test, up to 4,000 characters.

functions.name: GENERATE_SERIES
functions.summary: Returns a single-column table (value) of numbers from start to stop, stepping by step. (SQL Server 2022+)

params.name: start
params.doc: The first value of the series.

params.name: stop
params.doc: The last value; the series stops before passing it.

params.name: step
params.doc: The increment; default 1, or -1 when start is greater than stop.

functions.name: CONVERT
functions.summary: Converts a value to another data type, with an optional style number controlling date and number formats.

params.name: data_type [(length)]
params.doc: The target data type, with optional length, precision or scale.

params.name: style
params.doc: A style code such as 23 (yyyy-mm-dd), 103 (dd/mm/yyyy), 120 (ODBC canonical) or 126 (ISO 8601).

functions.name: TRY_CONVERT
functions.summary: Converts a value to another data type like CONVERT, but returns NULL instead of an error when the conversion fails.

params.name: data_type [(length)]
params.doc: The target data type, with optional length, precision or scale.

params.name: style
params.doc: A style code controlling date and number formats, as for CONVERT.

functions.name: TRY_CAST
functions.summary: Converts a value to another data type like CAST, but returns NULL instead of an error when the conversion fails.

params.name: expression AS data_type [(length)]
params.doc: The value, the AS keyword, then the target data type.

functions.name: PARSE
functions.summary: Converts a string to a date/time or number type using a .NET culture. Slower than CAST; use only for culture-aware parsing.

params.name: string_value AS data_type [USING culture]
params.doc: The string, AS, the target type, and an optional culture such as 'de-DE'.

functions.name: TRY_PARSE
functions.summary: Converts a string to a date/time or number type using a .NET culture, returning NULL when parsing fails.

params.name: string_value AS data_type [USING culture]
params.doc: The string, AS, the target type, and an optional culture such as 'en-US'.

functions.name: IIF
functions.summary: Returns one of two values depending on whether a boolean expression is true; shorthand for a simple CASE.

signatures.returns: highest-precedence type of true_value and false_value

params.name: true_value
params.doc: Returned when the condition is true.

params.name: false_value
params.doc: Returned when the condition is false or unknown.

functions.name: CHOOSE
functions.summary: Returns the item at a 1-based index from a list of values, or NULL when the index is out of range.

params.name: index
params.doc: The 1-based position of the value to return.

params.name: val_2
params.doc: The next value; more may follow.

keywords.name: TOP
keywords.doc: Limits the rows a query returns or a statement affects to the first n (or n percent). Use with ORDER BY for a predictable result.

keywords.name: PERCENT
keywords.doc: Makes TOP return the given percentage of rows instead of a count.

keywords.name: WITH TIES
keywords.doc: With TOP and ORDER BY, also returns any rows that tie with the last row on the ORDER BY values.

keywords.name: TIES
keywords.doc: Part of TOP ... WITH TIES, which includes rows tied with the last returned row.

keywords.name: OFFSET
keywords.doc: Skips the given number of rows before returning results; requires ORDER BY. Often paired with FETCH NEXT for paging.
keywords.syntax: ORDER BY ... OFFSET n ROWS [FETCH NEXT m ROWS ONLY]

keywords.name: FETCH
keywords.doc: In ORDER BY paging, limits rows after OFFSET; for cursors, retrieves a row from an open cursor.
keywords.syntax: OFFSET n ROWS FETCH {FIRST | NEXT} m ROWS ONLY | FETCH [NEXT | PRIOR | FIRST | LAST | ABSOLUTE n | RELATIVE n] FROM cursor [INTO @var, ...]

keywords.name: NEXT
keywords.doc: Used in FETCH NEXT (paging and cursors) and NEXT VALUE FOR (sequences).

keywords.name: ONLY
keywords.doc: Ends an OFFSET ... FETCH clause.

keywords.name: FIRST
keywords.doc: Used in OFFSET/FETCH FIRST paging and to fetch the first row of a scroll cursor.

keywords.name: LAST
keywords.doc: Fetches the last row of a scroll cursor.

keywords.name: PRIOR
keywords.doc: Fetches the row before the current row of a scroll cursor.

keywords.name: ABSOLUTE
keywords.doc: Fetches the row at an absolute position in a scroll cursor.

keywords.name: RELATIVE
keywords.doc: Fetches the row n rows before or after the current row of a scroll cursor.

keywords.name: APPLY
keywords.doc: Evaluates a table-valued expression for each row of the left input. Use CROSS APPLY or OUTER APPLY.

keywords.name: CROSS APPLY
keywords.doc: Joins each left row to the rows of a table-valued function or subquery evaluated for that row; rows with no result are dropped.
keywords.syntax: FROM t CROSS APPLY fn(t.col) AS x

keywords.name: OUTER APPLY
keywords.doc: Like CROSS APPLY, but keeps left rows that produce no result, filling the right columns with NULL.
keywords.syntax: FROM t OUTER APPLY (SELECT TOP (1) ...) AS x

keywords.name: PIVOT
keywords.doc: Rotates rows into columns by aggregating values for each listed column value.
keywords.syntax: FROM src PIVOT (aggregate(value_col) FOR pivot_col IN ([v1], [v2], ...)) AS p

keywords.name: UNPIVOT
keywords.doc: Rotates columns into rows, producing a name column and a value column.
keywords.syntax: FROM src UNPIVOT (value_col FOR name_col IN (col1, col2, ...)) AS u

keywords.name: FOR
keywords.doc: Introduces the pivot column in PIVOT/UNPIVOT, the output format in FOR XML/FOR JSON, trigger timing, SYSTEM_TIME queries, and cursor declarations.
keywords.syntax: FOR XML PATH | FOR JSON AUTO | FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF ... | FOR INSERT, UPDATE

keywords.name: WITHIN GROUP
keywords.doc: Specifies the sort order that STRING_AGG, PERCENTILE_CONT, PERCENTILE_DISC and the APPROX_PERCENTILE functions work over.

keywords.name: WITHIN
keywords.doc: Part of WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...), the ordering clause of ordered-set aggregates.

keywords.name: WINDOW
keywords.doc: Defines named window specifications that OVER clauses can refer to. (SQL Server 2022+)
keywords.syntax: WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY a ORDER BY b)

keywords.name: IS DISTINCT FROM
keywords.doc: Compares two values treating NULLs as equal to each other; IS NOT DISTINCT FROM is the null-safe equality test. (SQL Server 2022+)

keywords.name: TABLESAMPLE
keywords.doc: Returns an approximate random sample of a table's pages.

keywords.name: AT TIME ZONE
keywords.doc: Converts a date/time to a datetimeoffset in the named Windows time zone, or treats a local value as belonging to that zone.
keywords.syntax: OrderDate AT TIME ZONE 'Pacific Standard Time'

keywords.name: ZONE
keywords.doc: Part of AT TIME ZONE.

keywords.name: NEXT VALUE FOR
keywords.doc: Returns the next number from a sequence object.

keywords.name: OUTPUT
keywords.doc: Returns the rows changed by INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or MERGE using the inserted and deleted pseudo-tables; also marks a procedure parameter as an output parameter.

keywords.name: OUT
keywords.doc: Short form of OUTPUT for procedure parameters.

keywords.name: INSERTED
keywords.doc: Pseudo-table holding the new row values in triggers and OUTPUT clauses.

keywords.name: DELETED
keywords.doc: Pseudo-table holding the old row values in triggers and OUTPUT clauses.

keywords.name: OF
keywords.doc: Used in FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF, UPDATE OF (cursors), and similar clauses.

keywords.name: TO
keywords.doc: Target of GRANT, BACKUP, ALTER ... SWITCH, and the upper bound in FOR SYSTEM_TIME FROM ... TO.
keywords.syntax: GRANT SELECT ON t TO user | BACKUP DATABASE db TO DISK = 'path'

keywords.name: MERGE
keywords.doc: Inserts, updates or deletes target rows based on a join with a source; must end with a semicolon.
keywords.syntax: MERGE target USING source ON condition WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET ... WHEN NOT MATCHED [BY TARGET] THEN INSERT ... WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN DELETE;

keywords.name: MATCHED
keywords.doc: In MERGE, the condition that a source row found (or did not find) a matching target row.

keywords.name: WHEN MATCHED
keywords.doc: MERGE branch applied to target rows that match a source row.
keywords.syntax: WHEN MATCHED [AND condition] THEN {UPDATE SET ... | DELETE}

keywords.name: WHEN NOT MATCHED
keywords.doc: MERGE branch for source rows with no target match (BY TARGET, the default) or target rows with no source match (BY SOURCE).
keywords.syntax: WHEN NOT MATCHED [BY TARGET] THEN INSERT ... | WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN {UPDATE | DELETE}

keywords.name: SOURCE
keywords.doc: In MERGE, WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE targets rows that have no source match.
keywords.syntax: WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN DELETE

keywords.name: TARGET
keywords.doc: In MERGE, WHEN NOT MATCHED BY TARGET targets source rows missing from the target.
keywords.syntax: WHEN NOT MATCHED BY TARGET THEN INSERT ...

keywords.name: IF
keywords.doc: Runs a statement or BEGIN...END block when a condition is true, with an optional ELSE branch. Also IF EXISTS in DROP statements.
keywords.syntax: IF condition statement [ELSE statement] | DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t

keywords.name: WHILE
keywords.doc: Repeats a statement or block while a condition is true.

keywords.name: BREAK
keywords.doc: Exits the innermost WHILE loop.
keywords.syntax: WHILE ... BEGIN IF cond BREAK; END

keywords.name: CONTINUE
keywords.doc: Restarts the innermost WHILE loop, skipping the rest of its body.
keywords.syntax: WHILE ... BEGIN IF cond CONTINUE; ... END

keywords.name: RETURN
keywords.doc: Exits a batch, procedure or function immediately; procedures may return an integer status, functions return their value.

keywords.name: RETURNS
keywords.doc: Declares the return type of a user-defined function.
keywords.syntax: CREATE FUNCTION f(...) RETURNS type | TABLE AS ...

keywords.name: GOTO
keywords.doc: Jumps to a label defined in the same batch or procedure as label_name:.

keywords.name: WAITFOR
keywords.doc: Pauses execution for a duration (DELAY) or until a time of day (TIME), or waits for a Service Broker message.

keywords.name: DELAY
keywords.doc: Part of WAITFOR DELAY: pauses for the given duration, up to 24 hours.

keywords.name: BEGIN TRY
keywords.doc: Starts a TRY block; an error inside passes control to the following CATCH block.
keywords.syntax: BEGIN TRY ... END TRY BEGIN CATCH ... END CATCH

keywords.name: END TRY
keywords.doc: Ends a TRY block; must be followed immediately by BEGIN CATCH.

keywords.name: BEGIN CATCH
keywords.doc: Starts a CATCH block that runs when the preceding TRY block raises an error. Use ERROR_MESSAGE() and friends inside.

keywords.name: END CATCH
keywords.doc: Ends a CATCH block.

keywords.name: TRY
keywords.doc: Part of BEGIN TRY ... END TRY error handling.

keywords.name: CATCH
keywords.doc: Part of BEGIN CATCH ... END CATCH error handling.

keywords.name: THROW
keywords.doc: Raises an error and transfers control to a CATCH block; without arguments inside CATCH it re-throws the current error. The statement before must end with a semicolon.

keywords.name: RAISERROR
keywords.doc: Raises an error or informational message with a severity and state; supports printf-style substitution. Severity 10 or less is informational.
keywords.syntax: RAISERROR ({msg_id | 'msg_str' | @var}, severity, state [, argument ...]) [WITH {LOG | NOWAIT | SETERROR}]

keywords.name: PRINT
keywords.doc: Returns a user-defined message to the client as an informational message.

keywords.name: DECLARE
keywords.doc: Declares local variables, table variables or cursors; variables start as NULL unless initialized.
keywords.syntax: DECLARE @name type [= value] [, ...] | DECLARE @t TABLE (...) | DECLARE c CURSOR FOR select

keywords.name: EXEC
keywords.doc: Short form of EXECUTE: runs a stored procedure or a dynamic SQL string.

keywords.name: EXECUTE
keywords.doc: Runs a stored procedure, a function, or a string of dynamic SQL; with AT runs it on a linked server.

keywords.name: EXECUTE AS
keywords.doc: Switches the execution context to another user or login, or sets the context a module runs under.
keywords.syntax: EXECUTE AS {USER | LOGIN} = 'name' | WITH EXECUTE AS {CALLER | SELF | OWNER | 'user'}

keywords.name: REVERT
keywords.doc: Switches the execution context back to the caller after EXECUTE AS.

keywords.name: CALLER
keywords.doc: In WITH EXECUTE AS CALLER, runs the module as the calling user (the default).

keywords.name: SELF
keywords.doc: In WITH EXECUTE AS SELF, runs the module as the user who created or altered it.

keywords.name: OWNER
keywords.doc: In WITH EXECUTE AS OWNER, runs the module as its owner.

keywords.name: GO
keywords.doc: Batch separator recognized by client tools, not a T-SQL statement. GO n repeats the batch n times.

keywords.name: USE
keywords.doc: Changes the current database for the connection.

keywords.name: TRAN
keywords.doc: Short form of TRANSACTION.
keywords.syntax: BEGIN TRAN | COMMIT TRAN | ROLLBACK TRAN

keywords.name: SAVE
keywords.doc: Part of SAVE TRANSACTION, which sets a savepoint.

keywords.name: SAVE TRANSACTION
keywords.doc: Sets a savepoint inside a transaction that ROLLBACK TRANSACTION name can return to.

keywords.name: BEGIN TRANSACTION
keywords.doc: Starts an explicit transaction and increments @@TRANCOUNT.

keywords.name: DISTRIBUTED
keywords.doc: Part of BEGIN DISTRIBUTED TRANSACTION, which starts a transaction coordinated by MS DTC across servers.

keywords.name: WORK
keywords.doc: Optional word in COMMIT WORK and ROLLBACK WORK.

keywords.name: TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL
keywords.doc: Sets the locking and row-versioning behavior of the session's transactions.
keywords.syntax: SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL {READ UNCOMMITTED | READ COMMITTED | REPEATABLE READ | SNAPSHOT | SERIALIZABLE}

keywords.name: ISOLATION
keywords.doc: Part of SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL.

keywords.name: LEVEL
keywords.doc: Part of SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL.

keywords.name: READ
keywords.doc: Part of the READ COMMITTED, READ UNCOMMITTED and REPEATABLE READ isolation levels.
keywords.syntax: SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED

keywords.name: COMMITTED
keywords.doc: READ COMMITTED isolation: reads see only committed data (the default level).
keywords.syntax: SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED

keywords.name: UNCOMMITTED
keywords.doc: READ UNCOMMITTED isolation: reads may see uncommitted (dirty) data, like NOLOCK.
keywords.syntax: SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ UNCOMMITTED

keywords.name: REPEATABLE
keywords.doc: REPEATABLE READ isolation: rows read cannot be changed by others until the transaction ends. Also TABLESAMPLE REPEATABLE.
keywords.syntax: SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ

keywords.name: SERIALIZABLE
keywords.doc: SERIALIZABLE isolation (and table hint): range locks prevent other transactions inserting rows the query would read.
keywords.syntax: SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL SERIALIZABLE | WITH (SERIALIZABLE)

keywords.name: SNAPSHOT
keywords.doc: SNAPSHOT isolation (and table hint): reads see a consistent row-versioned view as of the start of the transaction.

keywords.name: CURSOR
keywords.doc: Declares a cursor for row-by-row processing of a query result; also the cursor data type for variables.
keywords.syntax: DECLARE name CURSOR [LOCAL | GLOBAL] [FORWARD_ONLY | SCROLL] [STATIC | KEYSET | DYNAMIC | FAST_FORWARD] FOR select_statement

keywords.name: OPEN
keywords.doc: Opens a declared cursor and populates it by running its query. Also OPEN SYMMETRIC KEY.

keywords.name: CLOSE
keywords.doc: Closes an open cursor, releasing its result set and locks; it can be reopened.

keywords.name: DEALLOCATE
keywords.doc: Removes a cursor reference; the cursor is freed when the last reference is removed.

keywords.name: LOCAL
keywords.doc: Cursor option: the cursor is visible only in the batch, procedure or trigger that declared it.

keywords.name: GLOBAL
keywords.doc: Cursor option: the cursor is visible to the whole connection.

keywords.name: FORWARD_ONLY
keywords.doc: Cursor option: rows can be fetched only from first to last.

keywords.name: SCROLL
keywords.doc: Cursor option: all fetch directions (FIRST, LAST, PRIOR, ABSOLUTE, RELATIVE) are allowed.

keywords.name: STATIC
keywords.doc: Cursor option: fetches from a snapshot copy of the result in tempdb; changes to base tables are not seen.

keywords.name: KEYSET
keywords.doc: Cursor option: membership and order are fixed when opened; changes to non-key values are visible.

keywords.name: DYNAMIC
keywords.doc: Cursor option: reflects all data changes made while the cursor is open.

keywords.name: FAST_FORWARD
keywords.doc: Cursor option: a FORWARD_ONLY, READ_ONLY cursor with performance optimizations. Good default for loops.
keywords.syntax: DECLARE c CURSOR LOCAL FAST_FORWARD FOR ...

keywords.name: READ_ONLY
keywords.doc: Cursor option: prevents updates through the cursor. Also a database option.

keywords.name: SCROLL_LOCKS
keywords.doc: Cursor option: locks rows as they are fetched so positioned updates are guaranteed to succeed.

keywords.name: OPTIMISTIC
keywords.doc: Cursor option: positioned updates fail if the row changed since it was fetched; rows are not locked.

keywords.name: INSENSITIVE
keywords.doc: ISO cursor option equivalent to STATIC.

keywords.name: PROCEDURE
keywords.doc: A stored procedure: a saved batch of T-SQL with parameters.
keywords.syntax: CREATE [OR ALTER] PROCEDURE name [@p type [= default] [OUTPUT], ...] AS BEGIN ... END

keywords.name: PROC
keywords.doc: Short form of PROCEDURE.

keywords.name: FUNCTION
keywords.doc: A user-defined scalar or table-valued function.
keywords.syntax: CREATE [OR ALTER] FUNCTION name (@p type, ...) RETURNS type AS BEGIN ... RETURN ... END

keywords.name: CREATE OR ALTER
keywords.doc: Creates the object, or alters it in place when it already exists (procedures, functions, views, triggers).
keywords.syntax: CREATE OR ALTER {PROCEDURE | FUNCTION | VIEW | TRIGGER} name ...

keywords.name: SCHEMA
keywords.doc: A namespace that owns tables, views and other objects.

keywords.name: DATABASE
keywords.doc: A database: a collection of schemas, objects and files.
keywords.syntax: CREATE DATABASE name | ALTER DATABASE name SET ... | USE name

keywords.name: SYNONYM
keywords.doc: An alternative name for a table, view, procedure or function, possibly on another database or server.

keywords.name: SEQUENCE
keywords.doc: A schema object that generates a sequence of numbers independent of any table.
keywords.syntax: CREATE SEQUENCE name [AS type] [START WITH n] [INCREMENT BY n] [MINVALUE n | NO MINVALUE] [MAXVALUE n | NO MAXVALUE] [CYCLE | NO CYCLE] [CACHE n | NO CACHE]

keywords.name: START
keywords.doc: Sequence option: the first value returned.

keywords.name: INCREMENT
keywords.doc: Sequence option: the step between values.

keywords.name: MINVALUE
keywords.doc: Sequence option: the lowest value the sequence can return.

keywords.name: MAXVALUE
keywords.doc: Sequence option: the highest value the sequence can return.

keywords.name: CYCLE
keywords.doc: Sequence option: restart from the minimum (or maximum) when the limit is reached.

keywords.name: CACHE
keywords.doc: Sequence option: how many values are preallocated in memory.

keywords.name: NO
keywords.doc: Negates an option, as in NO CYCLE, NO CACHE, NO ACTION or NO MINVALUE.

keywords.name: TYPE
keywords.doc: A user-defined data type or table type; also the TYPE directive of FOR XML.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TYPE name FROM base_type | CREATE TYPE name AS TABLE (...)

keywords.name: ASSEMBLY
keywords.doc: A .NET CLR assembly registered in the database.
keywords.syntax: CREATE ASSEMBLY name FROM 'path' WITH PERMISSION_SET = SAFE

keywords.name: LOGIN
keywords.doc: A server-level security principal.
keywords.syntax: CREATE LOGIN name {WITH PASSWORD = 'pwd' | FROM WINDOWS | FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER}

keywords.name: ROLE
keywords.doc: A database or server role that groups permissions.
keywords.syntax: CREATE ROLE name | ALTER ROLE name ADD MEMBER user

keywords.name: MEMBER
keywords.doc: Used when adding or removing role members.
keywords.syntax: ALTER ROLE role ADD MEMBER principal

keywords.name: AUTHORIZATION
keywords.doc: Names the owner of a schema or other securable.
keywords.syntax: CREATE SCHEMA s AUTHORIZATION dbo | ALTER AUTHORIZATION ON object TO principal

keywords.name: INSTEAD OF
keywords.doc: Trigger timing that replaces the triggering INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE; allowed on tables and views.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TRIGGER t ON view INSTEAD OF INSERT AS ...

keywords.name: INSTEAD
keywords.doc: Part of INSTEAD OF triggers.

keywords.name: AFTER
keywords.doc: Trigger timing that fires after the triggering statement succeeds (same as FOR).
keywords.syntax: CREATE TRIGGER t ON table AFTER INSERT, UPDATE AS ...

keywords.name: READONLY
keywords.doc: Required on table-valued parameters: the table cannot be modified inside the module.

keywords.name: VARYING
keywords.doc: Marks a cursor output parameter whose result set is built dynamically.

keywords.name: EXTERNAL
keywords.doc: Used for external tables, data sources, file formats and CLR modules (EXTERNAL NAME).
keywords.syntax: CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE ... | EXTERNAL NAME assembly.class.method

keywords.name: SCHEMABINDING
keywords.doc: Binds a view or function to the underlying objects so they cannot be changed in ways that break it; required for indexed views.
keywords.syntax: CREATE VIEW v WITH SCHEMABINDING AS ...

keywords.name: ENCRYPTION
keywords.doc: Obfuscates the text of a module in the catalog; also used in key and certificate DDL.
keywords.syntax: CREATE PROCEDURE p WITH ENCRYPTION AS ...

keywords.name: NATIVE_COMPILATION
keywords.doc: Compiles a module to native code for memory-optimized tables.
keywords.syntax: CREATE PROCEDURE p WITH NATIVE_COMPILATION, SCHEMABINDING AS BEGIN ATOMIC ... END

keywords.name: IDENTITY
keywords.doc: Makes a column auto-number its rows from a seed by an increment. In SELECT INTO, IDENTITY(type, seed, increment) creates a new identity column.

keywords.name: IDENTITY_INSERT
keywords.doc: Allows explicit values to be inserted into a table's identity column. Only one table per session can have it ON.

keywords.name: ROWGUIDCOL
keywords.doc: Marks a uniqueidentifier column as the table's row GUID column.

keywords.name: CLUSTERED
keywords.doc: An index that sorts and stores the table's rows by its key; a table can have only one.
keywords.syntax: CREATE CLUSTERED INDEX ix ON t (col) | PRIMARY KEY CLUSTERED (col)

keywords.name: NONCLUSTERED
keywords.doc: An index stored separately from the table rows, pointing back to them.
keywords.syntax: CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX ix ON t (col) INCLUDE (other)

keywords.name: COLUMNSTORE
keywords.doc: An index that stores data by column, for analytics and heavy compression.
keywords.syntax: CREATE [CLUSTERED | NONCLUSTERED] COLUMNSTORE INDEX ix ON t [(col, ...)]

keywords.name: INCLUDE
keywords.doc: Adds non-key columns to the leaf level of a nonclustered index so it covers more queries.
keywords.syntax: CREATE INDEX ix ON t (key) INCLUDE (col1, col2)

keywords.name: FILLFACTOR
keywords.doc: Percentage of each index leaf page filled when the index is built or rebuilt.

keywords.name: ONLINE
keywords.doc: Index option: build or rebuild while the table stays available for queries and changes.

keywords.name: REBUILD
keywords.doc: Rebuilds an index (or table) from scratch, removing fragmentation.
keywords.syntax: ALTER INDEX ix ON t REBUILD [WITH (...)]

keywords.name: REORGANIZE
keywords.doc: Defragments an index's leaf level in place; always online.
keywords.syntax: ALTER INDEX ix ON t REORGANIZE

keywords.name: DISABLE
keywords.doc: Disables an index or trigger (DISABLE TRIGGER), or a constraint via NOCHECK.
keywords.syntax: ALTER INDEX ix ON t DISABLE | DISABLE TRIGGER t ON table

keywords.name: ENABLE
keywords.doc: Re-enables a disabled trigger.

keywords.name: NOCHECK
keywords.doc: Disables a foreign key or check constraint, or adds one without validating existing rows.
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE t NOCHECK CONSTRAINT fk | ALTER TABLE t WITH NOCHECK ADD CONSTRAINT ...

keywords.name: CASCADE
keywords.doc: Referential action: deleting or updating a parent row does the same to its child rows. Also used by REVOKE and DENY.
keywords.syntax: FOREIGN KEY (col) REFERENCES p (id) ON DELETE CASCADE

keywords.name: ACTION
keywords.doc: Part of NO ACTION, the default referential action that rejects changes breaking a foreign key.

keywords.name: PERSISTED
keywords.doc: Stores a computed column's value physically so it can be indexed without recomputation.

keywords.name: SPARSE
keywords.doc: Optimizes storage of a column that is mostly NULL.

keywords.name: FILEGROUP
keywords.doc: A named group of database files that tables and indexes can be placed on.

keywords.name: REPLICATION
keywords.doc: Used in NOT FOR REPLICATION, which exempts replication agents from identity, constraint and trigger behavior.

keywords.name: SWITCH
keywords.doc: Moves a partition or whole table's data to another table instantly as a metadata operation.
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE src SWITCH [PARTITION n] TO target [PARTITION n]

keywords.name: TRUNCATE
keywords.doc: Removes all rows from a table (or partitions) quickly by deallocating pages; resets identity.

keywords.name: TRUNCATE TABLE
keywords.doc: Removes all rows from a table without logging individual row deletes. Fails when the table is referenced by a foreign key.

keywords.name: STATISTICS
keywords.doc: Distribution statistics used by the optimizer; also SET STATISTICS IO/TIME/XML/PROFILE for query diagnostics.
keywords.syntax: CREATE STATISTICS s ON t (col) | UPDATE STATISTICS t | SET STATISTICS IO ON

keywords.name: SYSTEM_VERSIONING
keywords.doc: Turns a table into a system-versioned temporal table that keeps full row history.

keywords.name: PERIOD
keywords.doc: Declares the pair of datetime2 columns that define a temporal table's validity period.

keywords.name: SYSTEM_TIME
keywords.doc: The period of a temporal table; FOR SYSTEM_TIME queries its history.
keywords.syntax: FOR SYSTEM_TIME {AS OF t | FROM t1 TO t2 | BETWEEN t1 AND t2 | CONTAINED IN (t1, t2) | ALL}

keywords.name: FOR SYSTEM_TIME
keywords.doc: Queries a temporal table as it was at a point in time or over a range.
keywords.syntax: FROM t FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF '2024-01-01T00:00:00'

keywords.name: CONTAINED
keywords.doc: In FOR SYSTEM_TIME CONTAINED IN (start, end), returns row versions that were open and closed within the range.

keywords.name: GENERATED ALWAYS
keywords.doc: Declares a column whose value the engine sets, such as temporal period columns or ledger columns.
keywords.syntax: ValidFrom datetime2 GENERATED ALWAYS AS ROW START

keywords.name: GENERATED
keywords.doc: Part of GENERATED ALWAYS AS ROW START/END column definitions.

keywords.name: ALWAYS
keywords.doc: Part of GENERATED ALWAYS.

keywords.name: HIDDEN
keywords.doc: Hides a period column from SELECT *.
keywords.syntax: ValidTo datetime2 GENERATED ALWAYS AS ROW END HIDDEN

keywords.name: MEMORY_OPTIMIZED
keywords.doc: Table option that stores the table in memory (In-Memory OLTP).

keywords.name: GRANT
keywords.doc: Gives a permission on a securable to a principal.
keywords.syntax: GRANT permission [, ...] ON securable TO principal [WITH GRANT OPTION]

keywords.name: REVOKE
keywords.doc: Removes a previously granted or denied permission.
keywords.syntax: REVOKE permission ON securable FROM principal [CASCADE]

keywords.name: DENY
keywords.doc: Explicitly denies a permission; a deny overrides any grant.
keywords.syntax: DENY permission ON securable TO principal [CASCADE]

keywords.name: PUBLIC
keywords.doc: The role every database user belongs to.
keywords.syntax: GRANT SELECT ON t TO public

keywords.name: CONTROL
keywords.doc: Permission granting full ownership-like rights on a securable.
keywords.syntax: GRANT CONTROL ON SCHEMA::s TO user

keywords.name: IMPERSONATE
keywords.doc: Permission to impersonate a user or login with EXECUTE AS.
keywords.syntax: GRANT IMPERSONATE ON USER::u TO other

keywords.name: CONNECT
keywords.doc: Permission to connect to a database or endpoint.

keywords.name: VIEW DEFINITION
keywords.doc: Permission to see an object's metadata and definition.
keywords.syntax: GRANT VIEW DEFINITION ON SCHEMA::dbo TO user

keywords.name: TAKE OWNERSHIP
keywords.doc: Permission to take ownership of a securable.
keywords.syntax: GRANT TAKE OWNERSHIP ON t TO user

keywords.name: OPTION
keywords.doc: Adds query hints to a statement.

keywords.name: RECOMPILE
keywords.doc: Compiles a fresh plan for each execution: as a query hint, or on a procedure with WITH RECOMPILE.
keywords.syntax: OPTION (RECOMPILE) | CREATE PROCEDURE p WITH RECOMPILE | EXEC p WITH RECOMPILE

keywords.name: MAXDOP
keywords.doc: Limits the number of processors used for a parallel plan.

keywords.name: MAXRECURSION
keywords.doc: Limits the recursion depth of a recursive CTE (default 100; 0 means no limit).

keywords.name: OPTIMIZE FOR
keywords.doc: Tells the optimizer which parameter values to optimize the plan for.

keywords.name: OPTIMIZE
keywords.doc: Part of the OPTIMIZE FOR query hint.

keywords.name: UNKNOWN
keywords.doc: In OPTIMIZE FOR UNKNOWN, optimizes using average statistics instead of sniffed parameter values.

keywords.name: FORCE ORDER
keywords.doc: Query hint: join tables in the order written.

keywords.name: FORCE
keywords.doc: Part of hints such as FORCE ORDER and FORCESEEK.

keywords.name: FAST
keywords.doc: Query hint: optimize for returning the first n rows quickly.

keywords.name: KEEPFIXED
keywords.doc: Query hint: do not recompile because of statistics changes.

keywords.name: PLAN
keywords.doc: Part of KEEP PLAN, KEEPFIXED PLAN and USE PLAN query hints.

keywords.name: KEEP
keywords.doc: Part of the KEEP PLAN query hint, which relaxes recompile thresholds for temp tables.

keywords.name: USE HINT
keywords.doc: Applies named query hints, such as 'DISABLE_PARAMETER_SNIFFING'.

keywords.name: HINT
keywords.doc: Part of the USE HINT query hint.

keywords.name: QUERYTRACEON
keywords.doc: Query hint: enable a trace flag for this statement only.

keywords.name: NOEXPAND
keywords.doc: Table hint: use an indexed view's index instead of expanding the view definition.

keywords.name: LOOP
keywords.doc: Join hint: use a nested loops join.

keywords.name: HASH
keywords.doc: Join or group hint: use a hash join or hash aggregate; also HASH indexes on memory-optimized tables.

keywords.name: REMOTE
keywords.doc: Join hint: perform the join on the site of the right table.

keywords.name: NOLOCK
keywords.doc: Table hint equal to READUNCOMMITTED: reads without shared locks and can see uncommitted, duplicated or missing rows.

keywords.name: READUNCOMMITTED
keywords.doc: Table hint: read uncommitted data without shared locks (same as NOLOCK).

keywords.name: READCOMMITTED
keywords.doc: Table hint: use READ COMMITTED semantics for this table.

keywords.name: READCOMMITTEDLOCK
keywords.doc: Table hint: use locking READ COMMITTED even when read committed snapshot is on.

keywords.name: REPEATABLEREAD
keywords.doc: Table hint: hold shared locks until the transaction ends.

keywords.name: HOLDLOCK
keywords.doc: Table hint equal to SERIALIZABLE: hold range locks until the transaction ends.

keywords.name: UPDLOCK
keywords.doc: Table hint: take update locks when reading so a later update in the transaction cannot deadlock.

keywords.name: XLOCK
keywords.doc: Table hint: take exclusive locks held until the transaction ends.

keywords.name: TABLOCK
keywords.doc: Table hint: take a table-level lock; enables minimal logging for bulk inserts.

keywords.name: TABLOCKX
keywords.doc: Table hint: take an exclusive table-level lock.

keywords.name: PAGLOCK
keywords.doc: Table hint: take page locks instead of row or table locks.

keywords.name: ROWLOCK
keywords.doc: Table hint: take row locks instead of page or table locks.

keywords.name: READPAST
keywords.doc: Table hint: skip rows locked by other transactions instead of waiting.

keywords.name: NOWAIT
keywords.doc: Table hint: fail immediately if a lock cannot be acquired. Also RAISERROR ... WITH NOWAIT sends the message at once.

keywords.name: FORCESEEK
keywords.doc: Table hint: use an index seek to access the table.

keywords.name: FORCESCAN
keywords.doc: Table hint: use a scan to access the table.

keywords.name: NOCOUNT
keywords.doc: SET NOCOUNT ON stops the 'n rows affected' messages, reducing network traffic.

keywords.name: XACT_ABORT
keywords.doc: SET XACT_ABORT ON rolls back the whole transaction when a run-time error occurs.

keywords.name: ANSI_NULLS
keywords.doc: SET ANSI_NULLS ON makes comparisons with NULL (= NULL) evaluate to unknown; required for many features.

keywords.name: ANSI_PADDING
keywords.doc: Controls how trailing blanks and zeros are stored in char, varchar, binary and varbinary columns.

keywords.name: ANSI_WARNINGS
keywords.doc: Controls ISO warnings for aggregates over NULL, divide-by-zero and truncation.

keywords.name: ARITHABORT
keywords.doc: Ends a query when an overflow or divide-by-zero error occurs.

keywords.name: CONCAT_NULL_YIELDS_NULL
keywords.doc: Controls whether concatenating NULL with a string returns NULL (ON, the standard) or the string.

keywords.name: QUOTED_IDENTIFIER
keywords.doc: SET QUOTED_IDENTIFIER ON makes double quotes delimit identifiers rather than strings.

keywords.name: NUMERIC_ROUNDABORT
keywords.doc: Controls whether loss of precision in an expression raises an error.

keywords.name: IMPLICIT_TRANSACTIONS
keywords.doc: When ON, data statements start a transaction automatically that must be committed explicitly.

keywords.name: DATEFIRST
keywords.doc: Sets the first day of the week, 1 (Monday) to 7 (Sunday); affects weekday calculations.

keywords.name: DATEFORMAT
keywords.doc: Sets the order of month, day and year parts when interpreting date strings.
keywords.syntax: SET DATEFORMAT {mdy | dmy | ymd | ydm | myd | dym}

keywords.name: LANGUAGE
keywords.doc: Sets the session language, which affects date names and formats. Also LANGUAGE in full-text predicates.

keywords.name: LOCK_TIMEOUT
keywords.doc: Sets how many milliseconds a statement waits for a lock; -1 waits forever.

keywords.name: DEADLOCK_PRIORITY
keywords.doc: Sets how likely the session is chosen as a deadlock victim.

keywords.name: ROWCOUNT
keywords.doc: SET ROWCOUNT stops processing after n rows (0 turns it off). Prefer TOP.

keywords.name: TEXTSIZE
keywords.doc: Sets the maximum bytes of varchar(max), nvarchar(max), varbinary(max), text and image data a SELECT returns.

keywords.name: NOEXEC
keywords.doc: SET NOEXEC ON compiles statements without running them.

keywords.name: PARSEONLY
keywords.doc: SET PARSEONLY ON checks syntax without compiling or running.

keywords.name: FMTONLY
keywords.doc: SET FMTONLY ON returns only result metadata, no rows. Deprecated; use sp_describe_first_result_set.

keywords.name: SHOWPLAN_XML
keywords.doc: SET SHOWPLAN_XML ON returns the estimated execution plan as XML instead of running statements.

keywords.name: SHOWPLAN_TEXT
keywords.doc: SET SHOWPLAN_TEXT ON returns the estimated execution plan as text instead of running statements.

keywords.name: SHOWPLAN_ALL
keywords.doc: SET SHOWPLAN_ALL ON returns detailed estimated plan rows instead of running statements.

keywords.name: IO
keywords.doc: SET STATISTICS IO ON reports logical and physical reads per table.

keywords.name: PROFILE
keywords.doc: SET STATISTICS PROFILE ON returns the actual execution plan as rows after each statement.

keywords.name: OFF
keywords.doc: Turns a SET option or database option off.

keywords.name: FOR XML
keywords.doc: Returns a query result as XML.
keywords.syntax: FOR XML {RAW | AUTO | EXPLICIT | PATH} [, TYPE] [, ROOT('name')] [, ELEMENTS]

keywords.name: FOR JSON
keywords.doc: Returns a query result as JSON text.
keywords.syntax: FOR JSON {AUTO | PATH} [, ROOT('name')] [, INCLUDE_NULL_VALUES] [, WITHOUT_ARRAY_WRAPPER]

keywords.name: PATH
keywords.doc: FOR XML PATH / FOR JSON PATH: shape the output with column aliases as paths.

keywords.name: AUTO
keywords.doc: FOR XML AUTO / FOR JSON AUTO: nest output automatically based on the tables in the SELECT.

keywords.name: RAW
keywords.doc: FOR XML RAW: one element per row.

keywords.name: EXPLICIT
keywords.doc: FOR XML EXPLICIT: build the XML shape from a universal table with Tag and Parent columns.

keywords.name: ROOT
keywords.doc: Adds a single top-level element or property around FOR XML or FOR JSON output.

keywords.name: ELEMENTS
keywords.doc: FOR XML option: return columns as sub-elements instead of attributes.

keywords.name: WITHOUT_ARRAY_WRAPPER
keywords.doc: FOR JSON option: omit the surrounding square brackets, for single-object output.

keywords.name: INCLUDE_NULL_VALUES
keywords.doc: FOR JSON option: include properties whose value is NULL.

keywords.name: BULK INSERT
keywords.doc: Loads a data file into a table.
keywords.syntax: BULK INSERT table FROM 'path' WITH (FORMAT = 'CSV', FIRSTROW = 2, FIELDTERMINATOR = ',')

keywords.name: BULK
keywords.doc: Part of BULK INSERT and OPENROWSET(BULK ...).

keywords.name: BACKUP
keywords.doc: Backs up a database, file or transaction log.
keywords.syntax: BACKUP {DATABASE | LOG} name TO DISK = 'path' [WITH COMPRESSION, ...]

keywords.name: RESTORE
keywords.doc: Restores a database, file or log from a backup.
keywords.syntax: RESTORE DATABASE name FROM DISK = 'path' [WITH REPLACE, RECOVERY, ...]

keywords.name: DISK
keywords.doc: Backup device type for a file path.

keywords.name: DBCC
keywords.doc: Database Console Commands for maintenance, validation and diagnostics.
keywords.syntax: DBCC CHECKDB | DBCC SHRINKFILE (...) | DBCC FREEPROCCACHE

keywords.name: KILL
keywords.doc: Ends a user session (and rolls back its work) by session ID.

keywords.name: CHECKPOINT
keywords.doc: Writes all dirty pages of the current database to disk.

keywords.name: RECONFIGURE
keywords.doc: Applies configuration changes made with sp_configure.

keywords.name: SHUTDOWN
keywords.doc: Stops the SQL Server instance.

types.name: bigint
types.doc: 8-byte integer from -2^63 to 2^63-1.

types.name: integer
types.doc: Synonym for int.

types.name: smallint
types.doc: 2-byte integer from -32,768 to 32,767.

types.name: tinyint
types.doc: 1-byte integer from 0 to 255.

types.name: bit
types.doc: Integer that is 1, 0 or NULL; the strings 'TRUE' and 'FALSE' convert to 1 and 0.

types.name: decimal
types.doc: Exact fixed-precision number with p total digits (1 to 38, default 18) and s digits after the decimal point (default 0).

types.name: dec
types.doc: Synonym for decimal.

types.name: numeric
types.doc: Exact fixed-precision number; functionally identical to decimal.

types.name: money
types.doc: Currency value with four decimal places, from about -922 trillion to 922 trillion (8 bytes).

types.name: smallmoney
types.doc: Currency value with four decimal places, from -214,748.3648 to 214,748.3647 (4 bytes).

types.name: float
types.doc: Approximate floating-point number; n of 1-24 gives 4-byte precision (real), 25-53 gives 8-byte (the default).

types.name: real
types.doc: 4-byte approximate floating-point number; same as float(24).

types.name: date
types.doc: Calendar date from 0001-01-01 to 9999-12-31 (3 bytes).

types.name: time
types.doc: Time of day with up to 100-nanosecond precision; fractional_seconds_precision 0 to 7 (default 7).

types.name: datetime
types.doc: Date and time from 1753-01-01 to 9999-12-31, rounded to .000, .003 or .007 seconds. Prefer datetime2 for new work.

types.name: datetime2
types.doc: Date and time from 0001-01-01 to 9999-12-31 with up to 100-nanosecond precision (default 7 digits).

types.name: datetimeoffset
types.doc: datetime2 value plus a time zone offset from -14:00 to +14:00.

types.name: smalldatetime
types.doc: Date and time from 1900-01-01 to 2079-06-06, accurate to the minute.

types.name: char
types.doc: Fixed-length non-Unicode text of n bytes (1 to 8000, default 1), padded with spaces.

types.name: character
types.doc: ISO synonym for char; character varying is a synonym for varchar.

types.name: varchar
types.doc: Variable-length non-Unicode text up to n bytes (1 to 8000), or up to 2 GB with max.

types.name: nchar
types.doc: Fixed-length Unicode text of n byte-pairs (1 to 4000, default 1).

types.name: nvarchar
types.doc: Variable-length Unicode text up to n byte-pairs (1 to 4000), or up to 2 GB with max. Literals use the N'...' prefix.

types.name: text
types.doc: Deprecated variable-length non-Unicode text up to 2 GB. Use varchar(max).

types.name: ntext
types.doc: Deprecated variable-length Unicode text up to 2 GB. Use nvarchar(max).

types.name: binary
types.doc: Fixed-length binary data of n bytes (1 to 8000, default 1).

types.name: varbinary
types.doc: Variable-length binary data up to n bytes (1 to 8000), or up to 2 GB with max.

types.name: image
types.doc: Deprecated variable-length binary data up to 2 GB. Use varbinary(max).

types.name: uniqueidentifier
types.doc: 16-byte GUID, generated by NEWID() or NEWSEQUENTIALID().

types.name: sql_variant
types.doc: Holds values of most other base types; use SQL_VARIANT_PROPERTY to inspect the stored type.

types.name: xml
types.doc: XML document or fragment up to 2 GB, optionally typed by an XML schema collection; queried with methods like .value() and .nodes().

types.name: json
types.doc: Native binary JSON document type. (SQL Server 2025+ and Azure SQL)

types.name: vector
types.doc: Array of floating-point numbers for embeddings and similarity search, with a fixed number of dimensions. (SQL Server 2025+ and Azure SQL)

types.name: cursor
types.doc: Data type for variables and output parameters that hold a reference to a cursor.

types.name: table
types.doc: Data type for table variables and multi-statement function results.

types.name: hierarchyid
types.doc: Variable-length position in a tree hierarchy, with methods such as GetAncestor() and IsDescendantOf().

types.name: geometry
types.doc: Planar (flat-earth) spatial data such as points, lines and polygons.

types.name: geography
types.doc: Ellipsoidal (round-earth) spatial data such as GPS latitude and longitude.

types.name: rowversion
types.doc: Automatically generated 8-byte binary number, unique within a database, that changes whenever the row changes. Used for optimistic concurrency.

types.name: timestamp
types.doc: Deprecated synonym for rowversion; it is not a date or time.

types.name: sysname
types.doc: System type for object names, equivalent to nvarchar(128) NOT NULL.
